### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A27 was present in every trace (200 of 200) and about 95 in 100 of A26's observed outgoing transitions went to A27. In the later window, A27 appears in only about half of the traces (about 103 of 200), and A26 now leads to A27 in about half of its observed transitions and to A32, A33 or A38 in the other half (about 15, 18 and 17 in 100 respectively). [OCC003, DIR006]
- A32, A33 and A38 were not observed in the earlier window; in the later window each takes part in about half of the traces (about 98–100 of 200). They occur together in about 49 in 100 traces, and each pair appears in both orders in similar shares (about 21–27 in 100 each way), so they run without a fixed order between them. [OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, REL028, REL029, REL030]
- In the later window, A27 and each of the new activities behave as alternatives: they co-occur in only about 1 in 100 traces or fewer, while each appears alone in about half of the traces. In the earlier window A27 always occurred and the new activities never did. [REL022, REL023, REL024]
- The new activities sit between A26 and A28: in the later window each of them leads mostly to the other new activities and to A28 (about a quarter to two-fifths of their observed transitions go to A28), A28 co-occurs with each of them in about 49–50 in 100 traces with the new activity executed first in about 48 in 100 of those, and the distance from A26 to A28 widened from typically 2 steps (about 90 in 100 before) to about 2 or 4 steps (about 50 and 46 in 100). When A27 does run, it still follows A26 and precedes A28. [DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, REL017, REL021, REL025, REL026, REL027, LAG003]
- A04 changed from a rare, late activity to a frequent, early one: it took part in about 19 in 100 traces before versus about 60 in 100 after, and its median event position moved from about 0.55 to about 0.17 of the trace. [OCC001, POS001]
- In the later window, A14 leads directly to A04 in about 54 in 100 of its observed transitions (about 4 in 100 before) while A14 to A15 fell from about 87 to about 44 in 100; A04 leads to A15 in about 87 in 100 of its observed transitions, A14 precedes A04 in about 56 in 100 traces, A14 followed by A04 within one step rose from about 57 to about 96 in 100, and the A14-to-A15 distance shifted from mostly one step to often two. [DIR004, DIR001, REL001, REL002, LAG001, LAG002]
- A06 became rarer, from about 20 in 100 traces to about 4 in 100, and its outgoing transitions now go to a different set of successors; the later profile rests on only 8 traces. [OCC002, DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, a group of three previously unobserved activities (A32, A33, A38) runs between A26 and A28 in about half of the traces, while A27 — previously always executed between A26 and A28 — is now skipped in about half of the traces; A27 and the new group act as alternatives, and the new activities run in no fixed order among themselves before A28. Screening flagged 55 control-flow items where fewer than one would be expected if nothing had changed, so the pattern as a whole is unlikely to be a sampling artefact. The main limitation is that zero participation in the earlier window strictly shows only that A32, A33 and A38 were not observed then; with 200 earlier traces, an activity occurring in half of them would be very unlikely to be missed entirely, but the evidence cannot formally exclude that these activities existed without being executed. [OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, REL017, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024, REL025, REL026, REL027, REL028, REL029, REL030, LAG003]

Other differences: A04 turned from a rare, late activity (about 19 in 100 traces, median position about 0.55) into a frequent, early one (about 60 in 100 traces, median position about 0.17) that now typically runs directly between A14 and A15 — A14 leads to A04 in about 54 in 100 of its transitions, A04 leads to A15 in about 87 in 100, and the A14-to-A15 distance shifted from mostly one step to often two — a second, separate change in how the A14-to-A15 path is executed. A06 also became rarer (about 20 to about 4 in 100 traces), though its later routing profile rests on only 8 traces and is therefore weak. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR004, REL001, REL002, LAG001, LAG002, OCC002, DIR002]

Now let me understand the behavioural story.

- OCC006 (A38): participation 0.0 → 0.49. New.

**DIR items:**

- DIR004 (A14): before A15 0.865 dominant; after A04 0.542 and A15 0.443. So A14 now leads to A04 about half the time. Support 200/201 — strong.

- DIR006 (A26): before A27 0.95 dominant; after A27 0.505, A33 0.18, A38 0.165, A32 0.15. So A26 now leads to the new activities A32/A33/A38 about half the time.
